title: 3-D Objects: Prisms, Pyramids, Cylinders, Cones and Nets
seo_title: Grade 5 3-D Objects Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise, visualise and name 3-D objects in the environment and geometric settings, focusing on rectangular prisms and other prisms, cubes, cylinders, cones and pyramids; describe, sort and compare 3-D objects in terms of shape of faces, number of faces, flat and curved surfaces; make 3-D models using cut-out polygons and nets.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 3-D objects worksheets: prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, faces, edges, vertices and nets. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Prisms are named after the end face, pyramids after the base.
key_sub: A net folds into the object.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A prism has two identical end faces joined by rectangles. It is named after its end face: triangular prism.
  • A pyramid has one base and triangles that meet at a point (apex). It is named after its base.
  • Cylinders, cones and spheres have curved surfaces.
  • A net is a flat shape that folds up to make the object.

Examples

Example

2 triangles and 3 rectangles

the end faces are triangles

Answer: a triangular prism

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Named after the sidesUse the end face or the base.
Faces you can seeCount the hidden faces too.
Overlapping netEach face needs its own place.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about 3-D objects?
faq.a: Recognise, visualise and name 3-D objects (spheres, cylinders, cones, prisms and pyramids), describe and compare their faces, and make 3-D models with nets.

faq.q: How many faces does a square-based pyramid have?

faq.a: Yes, a square prism with all faces equal.

items.q: Is this object a prism or a pyramid?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. The 2 triangle ends match, and 3 rectangles join them. Triangle faces do not always mean a pyramid.

items.q: What kind of object is this?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The square is the base, and 4 triangles meet at the top.

items.q: Which word describes this object?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. The top and bottom are matching hexagons, joined by 6 rectangles.

items.q: Is this object a prism or a pyramid?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). All 4 faces are triangles, and 3 of them meet at the top.

items.q: What kind of object is this?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. The front and back are matching shapes with 5 sides, joined by rectangles. The pointed roof does not make it a pyramid.

items.q: Which word describes this object?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The base has 5 sides, and 5 triangles meet at the top.

items.q: Is this object a prism or a pyramid?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. Every face is a rectangle. Any two opposite faces can be the bases.
It has 2 matching circles and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A prism has only flat faces, so a cylinder is not a prism.

items.q: Why is this object a pyramid?
c: It has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point
It has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles
items.e: The hexagon is the base, and 6 triangles meet at the apex. Having triangle faces is not enough: a triangular prism has triangles too.

items.q: Why is this object a prism?
c: It has 1 base and an apex
It has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles
items.e: The top and bottom are matching triangles, and 3 rectangles join them. A square pyramid also has 5 faces, so that is not the reason.

items.q: How many bases does a prism have?
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. 1 base belongs to a pyramid.

items.q: How many bases does a square pyramid have?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The square is the only base. The 4 triangles are side faces, and 5 is the number of faces in all.

items.q: In a prism, what shape are the faces that join the two bases?
c: the same shape as the bases
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. Triangles that meet at a point belong to a pyramid.

items.q: In a pyramid, what shape are the faces that are not the base?
c: the same shape as the base
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). Rectangles join the bases of a prism.

items.q: The point at the top of a pyramid, where the triangles meet, is called the …
items.e: The apex is the vertex where all the triangle faces meet. The base is the face opposite the apex.

items.q: Which object has an apex?
items.e: Only a pyramid has triangles that meet at one point. The prisms have 2 bases and no apex.

items.q: Zinhle says, “This object has triangle faces, so it must be a pyramid.” The object has 2 matching triangles joined by 3 rectangles. Is she right?
c: Yes, triangles always make a pyramid
items.e: A prism has 2 matching bases joined by rectangles. This object is a triangular prism. A pyramid has only 1 base, and its triangles meet at a point.

items.q: An object has 1 hexagon face and 6 triangle faces that meet at a point. What kind of object is it?
items.e: A pyramid has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point (the apex). The hexagon is the base, so it is a hexagonal pyramid.

items.q: Which object is a pyramid?
items.e: B has 1 base and triangles that meet at a point. The other objects have 2 matching bases joined by rectangles, so they are prisms.
A has 2 matching pentagon bases joined by rectangles. The others come to a point: two pyramids and a cone.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The 2 matching ends are triangles, so it is a triangular prism. It lies on a rectangle, but that face is not a base. Do not use its 5 faces: that would give “pentagonal”.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The bases are rectangles, so it is a rectangular prism. It has 6 faces, but “hexagonal” would mean hexagon bases. It is not a cube, because its faces are not all squares.

items.q: Which name is correct for this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. Count the sides of an end: 5 sides, so it is a pentagonal prism. 7 is its number of faces.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The end looks like a house: a square with a triangle on top. Count its sides: 5. So it is a pentagonal prism, not a triangular prism.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. Each end has 6 sides, so it is a hexagonal prism. 8 is its number of faces, and the rectangles are only the side faces.

items.q: Which name is correct for this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. This prism stands on a base. The top and bottom are matching pentagons, so it is a pentagonal prism.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. Each end has 8 sides, so it is an octagonal prism. 10 is its number of faces.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base is a triangle, so it is a triangular pyramid. All 4 faces are triangles. Do not name it by its 4 faces: that would give a 4-sided base.

items.q: Which name is correct for this object?
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base is a square, so it is a square pyramid. Do not name it by its triangle side faces or by its 5 faces.

items.q: Name this object.
items.e: Prisms and pyramids are named after the shape of the base. The base is a long rectangle, so it is a rectangular pyramid. The triangles are side faces, so they do not name it.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 6 squares, all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There are 6 squares, all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a rectangular prism.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a rectangular prism. Two faces are squares, but the other 4 are long rectangles, so it is not a cube.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs. They fold into a rectangular prism. The top and bottom are squares, but the 4 sides are thin rectangles, so it is not a cube.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles joining them. They fold into a triangular prism.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the ends) and 3 rectangles joining them. They fold into a triangular prism. The triangles do not have to be equilateral.

items.q: This net is folded up. What object does it make?
items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at a point. They fold into a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. One is the base and the other 3 meet at a point, so they fold into a triangular pyramid.

items.q: Which object does this net fold into?
items.e: There are 2 circles (the flat ends) and a rectangle that rolls up into the curved surface. They fold into a cylinder.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). You can see only 3 faces, but the bottom and the back end count too.

items.q: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). 3 edges round each end and 3 joining the ends.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3).

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces (2 rectangles + 4 rectangles), 12 edges (4 + 4 + 4) and 8 vertices (4 + 4). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: How many vertices does a pentagonal prism have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5).

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6). Do not forget the 6 edges that join the two ends.

items.q: How many vertices does a hexagonal prism have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6).

items.q: This is a square pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square + 4 triangles), 8 edges (4 round the base + 4 up to the apex) and 5 vertices (4 + 1 apex). Do not forget the square base on the bottom.

items.q: How many edges does a square pyramid have?
items.e: A square pyramid has 5 faces (1 square + 4 triangles), 8 edges (4 round the base + 4 up to the apex) and 5 vertices (4 + 1 apex).

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Vertices are the corners: 4 at the front and 4 at the back.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. You can see only 3 faces. The bottom, the back and one side are hidden, but they still count.

items.q: How many edges does a rectangular prism have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. There are 4 edges on the top, 4 on the bottom and 4 going up the sides.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Dashed lines show the edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. 3 edges round each triangle end and 3 long edges joining them: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. There are 3 corners on each triangle end: 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Do not forget the square base underneath.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 edges round the base and 4 going up to the top: 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 corners on the base and 1 at the top: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: This is a triangular pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Do not forget the triangle base underneath.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cube?
items.e: B folds into a cube with no gaps and no overlaps. Each of the others has two squares that fold onto the same face, so one face is left open.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cube?
items.e: C folds into a cube with no gaps and no overlaps. Each of the others has two squares that fold onto the same face, so one face is left open.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cube?
items.e: D folds into a cube with no gaps and no overlaps. Each of the others has two squares that fold onto the same face, so one face is left open.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cube?
items.e: A folds into a cube with no gaps and no overlaps. Each of the others has two squares that fold onto the same face, so one face is left open.

items.q: Which of these is a net of a cube?
items.e: C folds into a cube with no gaps and no overlaps. Each of the others has two squares that fold onto the same face, so one face is left open.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: D is not a net of a cube: two of its squares fold onto the same face, so one face of the cube is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: B is not a net of a cube: it has a 2-by-2 block of squares, but only 3 faces of a cube meet at a corner, so two squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: A is not a net of a cube: two of its squares fold onto the same face, so one face of the cube is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: B is not a net of a cube: it has a 2-by-2 block of squares, but only 3 faces of a cube meet at a corner, so two squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: D is not a net of a cube: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way round, so the first and last squares land on the same face. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face F?
items.e: Fold the net: face D lands opposite face F. A face that touches F in the net (C) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face F?
items.e: Faces F and B are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube with face B on the bottom. Which face is on the top?
items.e: Fold the net: face E lands opposite face B. A face that touches B in the net (D) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube with face B on the bottom. Which face is on the top?
items.e: Faces B and A are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face does NOT touch face F?
items.e: Fold the net: face B lands opposite face F. A face that touches F in the net (D, E) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a rectangular prism. Which face is opposite face Q?
items.e: Faces Q and S are the same size and have one face (R) between them in the strip, so they fold onto opposite sides. In a rectangular prism, opposite faces are always the same size and shape.

items.q: In the net, face B touches only 1 other face. When the net is folded into a cube, how many faces will touch face B?
items.e: On a cube, every face touches 4 other faces. Only the opposite face (face A) does not touch it.

items.q: This is a net of a dice. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 3. So the missing number is 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: This is a net of a dice. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 5. So the missing number is 7 − 5 = 2.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which 3 faces meet at the corner with the red dot?
items.e: Every corner of a cube is where 3 faces meet. In the net the dot touches B and C; when you fold the net, A folds up to the same corner, so the 3 faces are A, B and C.

items.q: Palesa’s pencil is a hexagonal prism. How many long flat faces run down its side (not counting the ends)?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides, so there are 6 rectangles along the pencil. 8 counts the 2 ends as well, and 3 is how many you can see at once.

items.q: A cereal box is a rectangular prism. Neo puts a sticker on every corner. How many stickers does he need?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 8 vertices: 4 on the top and 4 on the bottom. 6 is the number of faces and 12 the number of edges.

items.q: A gazebo in a park has a roof shaped like a hexagonal pyramid with no base. How many triangle panels make the roof?
items.e: A hexagonal pyramid has 1 triangle for each side of the hexagon: 6 triangles. 7 counts the base too, and 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: Nadia builds the frame of a square pyramid with straws, one straw for each edge. How many straws does she need?
items.e: 4 straws round the square base + 4 up to the apex = 8. 5 is the number of faces (and of vertices).

items.q: Amahle joins straws with balls of modelling clay at every corner of a triangular prism. How many balls of clay does she need?
items.e: One ball for each vertex: 3 on each triangle end, 3 + 3 = 6. 9 is the number of edges.

items.q: Sipho builds a birdhouse. The front and back are shaped like a house (a square with a triangle roof on top) and are joined by rectangles. What object is the birdhouse?
items.e: The house shape has 5 sides, so the birdhouse is a pentagonal prism.

items.q: In science class, a glass prism has 2 triangle ends. How many of its faces are rectangles?
items.e: A triangular prism has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles, one rectangle for each side of the triangle.

items.q: Pieter’s tea bag is shaped like a pyramid with 4 faces, all triangles. What is its name?
items.e: 4 triangle faces: 1 triangle base and 3 triangles that meet at a point. That is a triangular pyramid.

items.q: Karabo builds a cedar planter box shaped like a rectangular prism with no top. How many wooden faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces. With no top, there are 6 − 1 = 5: the bottom and 4 sides.

items.q: Lungile polishes every face of a glass paperweight shaped like a square pyramid. How many faces does he polish?
items.e: 1 square base + 4 triangles = 5 faces. 4 forgets the base, and 8 is the number of edges.

items.q: Andile makes a gift box shaped like a rectangular prism, with a lid. How many rectangles does he need in the net?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces: top (the lid), bottom and 4 sides. 8 is the number of vertices.

items.q: Kagiso makes an open box (a cube with no lid) to hold pencils. How many squares are in the net?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, but there is no lid, so the net has 6 − 1 = 5 squares.

items.q: A cereal box is a rectangular prism. It is 20 cm wide, 30 cm tall and 6 cm deep. How many faces of the box measure 20 cm by 30 cm?
items.e: The front and the back are both 20 cm by 30 cm. Opposite faces of a rectangular prism are the same size.

items.q: Sibusiso cuts out a net of a cube (6 squares in one piece) and folds it. How many edges must he tape to close the cube?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges. The 6 squares of the net are joined by 5 folds, so 12 − 5 = 7 edges are still open and need tape.

items.q: A net of a square-based pyramid (a square with a triangle on each side) is folded up. How many edges need tape?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges. The 4 triangles are joined to the square by 4 folds, so 8 − 4 = 4 edges need tape.

items.q: A camping tent is a triangular prism with a floor. How many pieces of fabric are needed if each face is one piece?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangles (2 sloping sides and the floor).

items.q: A play tent has the shape of a triangular prism, but it has no floor. How many faces of fabric does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces. Without the floor there are 5 − 1 = 4: 2 triangle ends and 2 sloping sides.

items.q: The frame of a play tent has a pole along every edge of a triangular prism. How many poles are there?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges: 3 round each triangle end and 3 long edges joining them.

items.q: A chocolate bar comes in a long box shaped like a triangular prism. Which shapes are in the net of the box?
items.e: The 2 triangles are the ends of the box and the 3 rectangles are its long sides.

items.q: The ends of a triangular chocolate box are triangles with all 3 sides 4 cm. The box is 20 cm long. What size is each rectangle in the net?
items.e: Each rectangle is as wide as one side of the triangle (4 cm) and as long as the box (20 cm), so it is 4 cm by 20 cm.
